Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) and his Family Members Endures Hardships and Difficulties
Rasulullaah ﷺ Gives Glad Tidings of Jannah to Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) and his Family when he sees them being Tortured

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by Hadhrat Ammar (RA) and his family (his parents) as they were being tortured by the Mushrikeen, he said, "O family of Yaasir! Hear the glad tidings that your promised abode shall be Jannah."[^2]

Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) narrates that he was once walking with Rasulullaah ﷺ in Bat'haa (a rocky area of Makkah) when they saw Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) and his parents being tortured in the sun to make them forsake Islaam. Hadhrat Ammaar (RA)'s father (Yaasir (RA)) cried, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! This has been happening forever." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Be patient, O family of Yaasir. O Allaah! Forgive the family of Yaasir, which You have most certainly already done."[^3]
Hadhrat Sumayya (RA) the mother of Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) Becomes the First Martyr in Islaam

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by Hadhrat Ammar (RA) and his family (his parents) as they were being tortured by the Mushrikeen, he said, "Be patient, O family of Yaasir. Be patient, O family of Yaasir for your promised abode is Jannah."[^4] The narration of Hadhrat Kalbi states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Yaasir (RA) was also being tortured (with his brother Hadhrat Ammaar and his parents (RA)). The narration also adds that Hadhrat Sumayya (RA) was martyred when Abu Jahal pierced his spear into the most private part of her body. Hadhrat Yaasir (RA) was martyred during the torture and (his son) Abdullaah fell (dead) when an arrow was fired at him.[^5]
Hadhrat Mujaahid stated, "The first martyr was Hadhrat Sumayya (RA) the
Tabraani, Haakim, Bayhaqi and Ibn Asaakir. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.293) has commented on the chain of narrators.

Haakim in his Kuna, Ibn Asaakir, Ahmad, Bayhaqi, Baghawi, Uqayli, Ibn Mandah, Abu Nu'aym and others as reported in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.72). Ibn Sa'd has also narrated it in his Tabaqaat (Vol.3 Pg.177) from Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA).
Haakim Qazweeni. Ibn Kalbi has also reported the narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA).
